sentences.text: The applicant was enlarged on bail.
During the pendency of the proceedings, an application came to be filed by the applicant under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

In response to the said application and opposing the said request,
objections/reply were filed by Opposite Party.
The application filed by the applicant and the reply filed by Opposite Party No.2 are contained in Annexures - 3 & 4 (wrongly numbered as Annexures - 1 & 2).
It was informed at the Bar that the application under Section 207 Cr.P.C. came to be dismissed on 21.12.2023.

On account of objections filed by the Opposite Party, the applicant filed an application for punishing the objector/opposite party under Section 218 of IPC on 06.11.2023 which is contained in Annexure - 2.

In terms of the said application, it was argued that while filing the objection to the application under Section 207 Cr.P.C., the Opposite Party had disclosed wrong facts and thus, he should be summoned and should be tried for the commission of the offence under Section 218 of IPC.
The said application came to be rejected by means of the order dated 21.12.2023 holding the same to be not maintainable.

3. Challenging the said order dated 21.12.2023, the submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that in terms of the objections filed, a clear case for the offence under Section 218 of IPC was made out, as such, the trial Court was duty bound to summon the Opposite Party and to try him for the offence under Section 218 of the IPC.

4. It is necessary to refer to Section 218 of the IPC, which is as under:
"218. Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture.-- Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the preparation of any record or other writing, frames that record or writing in a manner which he knows to be incorrect,
with intent to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, loss or injury to the public or to any person, or with intent thereby to save, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby save, any person from legal punishment, or with intent to save, or knowing that he is likely thereby to save, any property from forfeiture or other charge to which it is liable by law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both."
5.

The submission made by counsel for the applicant merits rejection for the following reasons:
5.1

In terms of the mandate of Code of Criminal Procedure, proceedings for trying for an offence committed under the Indian Penal Code can be initiated, as prescribed under Chapter XII by filing an application under Section 154, or by an application under Section 156(3), or by filing a complaint as prescribed under Chapter XV.

5.2 In the present case, it is alleged by the applicant that by filing objection, the Opposite Party has committed the offence under Section 218 of IPC, however, there is no application/information traceable to Chapter XII or Chapter XV of the Cr.P.C.

The application filed by the applicant in the manner would not be an appropriate Harish Chandra vs Sabhajeet Chauhan Inspector Of Police, ... on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25071780/
2 application/information which is prescribed under Chapter XII or Chapter XV.

on that ground alone, I do not see any infirmity in the order passed by the trial Court.
6. In view thereof, the present application merits rejection and is accordingly rejected.
7. The trial Court is directed to ensure that the trial, which is pending since long, is concluded at the earliest without giving any unnecessary adjournment to any of the parties.
